title: Therapeutic Communication with Aphasia
learning_goal: Apply therapeutic communication techniques and referent communication models to overcome emotional and physical communication barriers.
target_audience: Nursing students and newly licensed nurses
visual_style: 2D semi-flat limited-animation style with dynamic but constrained movement. Mouth movement should suggest speech without matching every phoneme.

appearance.uniform: Navy blue scrubs with a stethoscope around the neck

appearance.distinguishing_features: Slight right-sided facial droop, primarily uses left hand to gesture

lighting.source: Bright daylight from the window and soft overhead room lights

setting.scene_description: A standard private hospital room. There is a bed in the center, a side table, and a large window with open blinds letting in bright sunlight.

scenes.scene_summary: Alex enters the room and observes Mr. Henderson struggling to communicate due to expressive aphasia following a stroke.
scenes.character_actions: Alex walks to the bedside. Mr. Henderson points at his head, making frustrated grunting noises, and hits the mattress with his left hand.

camera.movement: Slow pan from Alex to Mr. Henderson

dialogue.line: Good morning, Mr. Henderson. I'm Alex, your nurse. How are you feeling today?
My... the... ugh! No, not the... argh!

audio.sound_effects: Rustling of bedsheets, a frustrated hand smack against the mattress
audio.ambience: Low hum of medical equipment, distant hallway murmurs

scenes.scene_summary: Alex uses nontherapeutic interrogation, which makes the patient defensive.
scenes.character_actions: Alex questions the patient. Mr. Henderson glares, waves his hand dismissively, and turns his face away toward the wall.

dialogue.line: Why are you getting so upset? We will figure it out.

scenes.scene_summary: Alex uses therapeutic communication by sharing observations and offering silence.
scenes.character_actions: Alex speaks calmly. Mr. Henderson takes a deep breath, his face softens. He nods, points to his head, and then points toward the bright window.

camera.movement: Slight zoom in on Mr. Henderson

dialogue.line: It looks like you are frustrated. Take your time, I am here to listen.

scenes.scene_summary: Alex uses false reassurance and changes the subject, devaluing the patient's feelings.
scenes.character_actions: Alex smiles falsely. Mr. Henderson shakes his head vigorously, pushes an imaginary cup away, and crosses his arms.

dialogue.line: Don't worry, everything will be all right. I'll just get you some water.

scenes.scene_summary: Alex tries to decode Mr. Henderson's gestures about his head and the window.
scenes.character_actions: Alex stands attentively. Mr. Henderson nods eagerly but looks strained as he squints at the bright sunlight coming through the window.

camera.movement: Slow pan to the bright window and back

dialogue.line: You're pointing to your head and the window. Let's figure this out together.

scenes.scene_summary: Alex misunderstands the physical barrier and speaks loudly, frustrating the patient.
scenes.character_actions: Alex leans in and exaggerates mouth movements. Mr. Henderson recoils, covers his ears, and shakes his head in annoyance.

camera.angle: Close-up on Alex, then quick cut to Mr. Henderson

scenes.scene_summary: Alex rapid-fires questions, causing an information overload.
scenes.character_actions: Alex lists options quickly. Mr. Henderson looks overwhelmed, rubs his forehead, and closes his eyes to shut out the noise.

dialogue.line: Do you want the TV on? Are you hungry? Do you want me to call your wife?

scenes.scene_summary: Alex uses referent communication with a picture board to successfully interpret the patient's needs.
scenes.character_actions: Alex holds up a communication board. Mr. Henderson points to a 'headache' icon, then to the 'blinds' icon. Alex nods and moves to lower the blinds. Mr. Henderson smiles and gives a thumbs-up.

camera.movement: Slow zoom in on the communication board and Mr. Henderson's hand

dialogue.line: Can you point to what you need on this board?
You have a headache and want the blinds closed? I can do that, and I'll check your pain medication.

audio.sound_effects: Sound of window blinds being pulled down
audio.ambience: Low hum of medical equipment, transitioning to a quieter atmosphere

decision_points.question_text: How should Alex respond to Mr. Henderson's frustration while applying therapeutic communication techniques?

choices.text: It looks like you are frustrated. Take your time, I am here to listen.
Why are you getting so upset? We will figure it out.
choices.misconception: Asking 'why' questions is a nontherapeutic interrogating technique that makes the patient feel defensive.

choices.text: Don't worry, everything will be all right. I'll just get you some water.
choices.misconception: Giving false reassurance and changing the subject are nontherapeutic techniques that devalue the patient's concerns.

decision_points.question_text: Which strategy should Alex use to clarify the patient's needs, considering his physical communication barrier?

choices.text: Use a visual communication board and ask simple yes/no questions.
Speak louder and slower, asking him to repeat the words until he gets them right.
choices.misconception: Speaking louder does not help with aphasia, which is an expressive language barrier, not a hearing deficit.

choices.text: Ask a rapid series of questions: 'Do you want the TV on? Are you hungry? Do you need your wife?'
choices.misconception: Asking multiple questions rapidly causes a volume of information overload, which acts as a barrier to communication.
